newsitem.title: USA: Pentagon raises submarine cost estimate $2.1 bln.
newsitem.headline: Pentagon raises submarine cost estimate $2.1 bln.

text.p: The Defense Department said Tuesday that a new plan for two shipyards instead of one to develop and build the Navy's next attack submarine added more than $2 billion to its estimated cost.

It said in a new quarterly report on major U.S. weapons costs that the cost of 30 of the attack submarines to be built beginning next year was estimated at the end of last year to be $67 billion, $2.1 more than previous estimates.
The new submarine is to be built jointly by General Dynamics Corp's Electric Boat Division at Groton, Conn., and Newport News Shipbuilding Inc in Virginia.
The report said the cost increase was "due primarily to a revised procurement profile caused by a change in the acquisition strategy from single source to a teaming arrangement."

The Navy originally planned to have Electric Boat develop the submarine and then have the two shipyards share construction of it. But Congress ordered the submarine to be developed and built by both shipyards.

In February, after the September-December 1996 quarter covered by the new report, the two companies announced they would cut costs with a plan backed by the Navy for each of them to build segments of the submarines and then assemble them at one of the yards.
